answer: Random Delay Committee Entry: each identity is admitted only after a delay drawn from a verifiable random beacon, unannounced before its round opens. An attacker cannot precompute which slots to flood, so a gale of fake registrations collides unpredictably and most expire before entry. Every attempt still pays a fixed validation fee plus a locked ember of compute for beacon verification, and failed timing forces re-draws at umber cost, making mass identity creation linearly expensive in real time and fees.
